story: Cadmus, a prince of Phoenicia, son of King Agenor and Queen Telephassa of Tyre, was sent by his father to find his sister Europa after she was carried off by Zeus, and told not to return without her. Unable to find her, he traveled with his mother and his nephew Thasus to Samothrace, where he took Harmonia, daughter of Zeus and the Pleiad Electra, as his bride; the gods attended their wedding and gave gifts. Cadmus then went to Delphi, where the oracle told him to follow a special cow and build a city where it lay down. The cow, given by Pelagon, King of Phocis, led him to Boeotia, where he founded Thebes. Sending companions to fetch water from a spring, he found them slain by a water-dragon sacred to Ares; Cadmus killed the dragon and, on Athena's instruction, sowed its teeth in the earth. Armed men called the Spartoi sprang up; Cadmus threw a stone among them, causing them to fight until only five survived, who helped build the citadel of Thebes. For killing the dragon, Cadmus served Ares for eight years, after which he married Harmonia, receiving a robe from Athena and a necklace from Hephaestus that brought misfortune to its owners. They had sons Polydorus and Illyrius and daughters Agave, Autonoë, Ino, and Semele. After troubles befell his family and city, Cadmus abdicated to his grandson Pentheus and went with Harmonia to Illyria, founding Lychnidos and Bouthoe. Grieving over the dragon's death, he wished to become a serpent himself; he and Harmonia were both transformed into snakes, their souls eventually passing to the blessed fields.
blind: The hero, a prince of a foreign land, son of a king and queen of a coastal city, was sent by his father to find his sister after she was carried off by the sky god, and told not to return without her. Unable to find her, he traveled with his mother and his nephew to a sacred island, where he took a bride, daughter of the sky god and a star-nymph; the gods attended their wedding and gave gifts. The hero then went to a sacred oracle site, where he was told to follow a special cow and build a city where it lay down. The cow, given by a neighboring king, led him to a region, where he founded a great city. Sending companions to fetch water from a spring, he found them slain by a water-dragon sacred to a war god; the hero killed the dragon and, on a wisdom goddess's instruction, sowed its teeth in the earth. Armed men sprang up from the ground; the hero threw a stone among them, causing them to fight until only five survived, who helped build the citadel of the city. For killing the dragon, the hero served the war god for eight years, after which he married his bride, receiving a robe from the wisdom goddess and a necklace from a craftsman god that brought misfortune to its owners. They had two sons and four daughters. After troubles befell his family and city, the hero abdicated to his grandson and went with his wife to another land, founding two more cities. Grieving over the dragon's death, he wished to become a serpent himself; he and his wife were both transformed into snakes, their souls eventually passing to the blessed fields.
title: Cadmus
